14	 *    `my_med` entry per medicine on the list, including ones marked stopped. Each save restates the
15	 *    whole list and `supersedes` the previous list item. `effective` is the date of the save.

43	  type: 'bp_reading';
44	
45	  /** When the cuff took the reading (cuff clock, synced to the phone), or when the patient says it was taken if typed. Local wall time. */
46	  measured_at: LocalDateTime;
47	
48	  /** Systolic pressure, mmHg. */

52	  diastolic_mmhg: number;

57	  /**

59	   * - 'cuff_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth cuff. Values are exactly what the cuff measured.
60	   * - 'typed': typed in by the patient (e.g. cuff not paired, or a reading taken elsewhere such as a
61	   *   pharmacy kiosk). Typos happen; the patient may later fix them, which produces a superseding day page.
62	   * A patient who types in a reading the cuff also synced produces two entries for one measurement;
63	   * HomeLog does not detect this.

66

88	   * The unit is a meter setting, so it **can change partway through one patient's history** (for

90	   */

103	   * - 'before_meal': before a meal other than breakfast-fasting.

111	   * - 'meter_sync': sent by a paired Bluetooth meter.

136	   * - 'skipped': the patient deliberately did not take it. See `skip_reason`.
137	   */

143	  /**
144	   * Unit for `amount`, from a fixed app list.
145	   * - 'units': insulin units (UCUM `[iU]`).
146	   * - 'tablets': number of tablets or capsules; the strength is on the My Medicines entry.
147	   * - 'puffs', 'mL': as named.
148	   * Present exactly when `amount` is present.
149	   */

165	
166	  /**
167	   * Symptom tags the patient picked from HomeLog's list. Empty when the note is not about a symptom.

228	/**
229	 * Consumer views, version 1: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
230	 *
231	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
232	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
233	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
234	 * what the source records.
235	 *
236	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
237	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
238	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
239	 * date.
240	 *
241	 * Conventions for every view:
242	 *
243	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
244	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
245	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
246	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
247	 *   below says otherwise.
248	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer displays everything in America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time"
249	 *   below mean wall-clock date/time in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight time).
250	 * - **Partial dates.** `PartialDate` strings keep the precision the source actually knows: "2016"
251	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.
252	 * - **Only what the source records.** Rows come from structured payload entries. Narrative text may be
253	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
254	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
255	 *   can show the source text behind a fact.
256	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.
257	 */
258	
259	/** A FOLIO record item in its JSON form (see the FOLIO record-item spec). */
260	export interface FolioItem {
261	  folio: string;
262	  /** Item id (ULID), unique within the issuer. */
263	  id: string;
264	  /** did:web of the issuing organization. */
265	  issuer: string;
266	  /** Patient id at this issuer. */
267	  patient: string;
268	  /** When the clinical event happened: RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a full or partial date. */
269	  effective: string;
270	  effective_end?: string;
271	  /** When the issuer committed this item: RFC 3339 date-time with offset. */
272	  recorded: string;
273	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
274	  /** The payload's schema: `type` names the entry type in the source's .d.ts. */
275	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
276	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that this item replaces entirely. */
277	  supersedes?: string[];
278	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that were entered in error, withdrawn without replacement. */
279	  retracts?: string[];
280	  /** Markdown narrative with `<ref id="…">…</ref>` spans; "" if none. */
281	  narrative: string;
282	  /** Entry id -> entry, each entry typed by the source's schema; {} if none. */
283	  payload: Record<string, any>;
284	}
285	
286	/** The mapper's entry point. `asOf` is a local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
287	export type Transform = (items: FolioItem[], asOf: string) => ViewRows;
288	
289	/** Everything one mapper returns for one patient and one source. Empty arrays where the source has nothing. */
290	export interface ViewRows {
291	  medications: MedicationRow[];
292	  problems: ProblemRow[];
293	  allergies: AllergyIntoleranceRow[];
294	  labs: LabResultRow[];
295	  vitals: VitalRow[];
296	}
297	
298	/** `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; the precision is the string's length. */
299	export type PartialDate = string;
300	
301	/** The items (and entries inside them) a row was built from. At least one. */
302	export type Evidence = { item_id: string; entry_id?: string }[];
303	
304	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
305	// Medications
306	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
307	
308	/**
309	 * One outpatient (home) medication as this source records it, with its status as of `asOf`.
310	 *
311	 * - One row per drug ingredient. If the source has several lines, orders or prescriptions for the
312	 *   same ingredient over time (stopped and restarted, re-entered), report the most recent one, i.e.
313	 *   the one whose own latest event is latest. A line or order that was entered in error, voided or
314	 *   retracted never existed: do not report it, and do not let it affect another line.
315	 * - Include medications that are stopped (status 'stopped') if the source still shows them, so the
316	 *   consumer can say what was stopped and why.
317	 * - Exclude hospital-only orders (infusions, IV fluids, inpatient-only drugs). They are not home
318	 *   medications.
319	 * - When the source publishes a medication list as repeated snapshots (each document or save restates
320	 *   the list), the latest in-scope snapshot is the source's list; a drug missing from the latest
321	 *   snapshot is not reported. When the source publishes events or status rows, the latest event or
322	 *   status row for a line determines its state, however old it is.
323	 */
324	export interface MedicationRow {
325	  /**
326	   * Generic ingredient name, lower case, without salt or form: "losartan" (not "losartan potassium"),
327	   * "metformin", "insulin glargine", "empagliflozin". Translate brand names the record uses
328	   * ("Jardiance" -> "empagliflozin"). Omit only when the record does not say which drug it is (e.g. the
329	   * patient wrote "water pill").
330	   */
331	  ingredient?: string;
332	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, only when the source states an ingredient-level RxNorm code. Never guessed or derived from a product code. */
333	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
334	  /** The drug as the source names it (display text), e.g. "losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet" or "Jardiance". */
335	  drug_name: string;
336	  /**
337	   * Status as of `asOf`, by this source's account.
338	   * - 'active': the patient should be taking it (or, on a patient's own list, says they are).
339	   * - 'held': paused with intent (or at least possibility) of resuming; the patient should not be
340	   *   taking it now. Not the same as stopped.
341	   * - 'stopped': discontinued.
342	   * - 'unknown': the source lists the drug but records no decision about whether it is being taken
343	   *   (e.g. a hospital list marked as not reconciled).
344	   */
345	  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
346	  /**
347	   * Local date on which the current status began according to this source: for 'held' or 'stopped',
348	   * the date of the hold or stop; for 'active', the date the source's current line or order started
349	   * (or resumed). Keep the source's precision. Omit if the source does not say.
350	   */
351	  status_since?: PartialDate;
352	  /**
353	   * Amount per administration currently prescribed (for 'held' and 'stopped': the amount when it was
354	   * held or stopped). For a patient's own list: the amount the patient says they take, if they give
355	   * one. `unit` is one of the listed units; convert source spellings ("unit", "UNT", "[iU]" ->
356	   * "units"; "tab"/"tablets" -> "tablet"). Omit when the source gives no single amount.
357	   */
358	  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
359	  /**
360	   * How often, normalized: 'QD' once daily, 'BID' twice daily, 'TID' three times daily, 'QHS' once
361	   * daily at bedtime, 'QW' once weekly, 'PRN' as needed, 'other' anything else. Omit if unknown.
362	   */
363	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'QW' | 'PRN' | 'other';
364	  /**
365	   * For 'stopped' rows, why, when the source records a coded or clearly stated reason:
366	   * - 'adverse_reaction': side effect or adverse reaction.
367	   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
368	   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by another drug for the same purpose.
369	   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
370	   * - 'patient_choice': the patient declined or asked to stop.
371	   * - 'other': another reason (see `status_reason_text`).
372	   * Omit when the source gives no reason, and on rows that are not 'stopped'.
373	   */
374	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
375	  /** Free-text reason for the current status (hold or stop) as the source wrote it, if any. */
376	  status_reason_text?: string;
377	  /** True when the row comes from the patient's own account (a self-reported list), not a clinician's record. */
378	  patient_reported: boolean;
379	  /** True when the source says the drug was bought without a prescription. Omit otherwise. */
380	  otc?: boolean;
381	  evidence: Evidence;
382	}

384	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
385	// Problems
386	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

388	/**
389	 * One condition on the source's problem list (or the source's equivalent: its diagnosis or history
390	 * lists), with status as of `asOf`.
391	 *
392	 * - One row per condition. Several entries for the same condition (re-listed in several documents,
393	 *   restaged, re-coded) are one row whose fields reflect the latest entry.
394	 * - Report only conditions the source asserts the patient has or had. Never report a condition that
395	 *   was ruled out, or one that was only suspected (working/provisional) and never confirmed.
396	 * - Billing codes attached to a visit or claim are not problem-list entries, unless the source says
397	 *   its problem list is built from them.
398	 * - An adverse effect of a drug (however the source records it, including as an ICD-10 T-code
399	 *   diagnosis) is an `AllergyIntoleranceRow` of type 'adverse_reaction', not a problem. The illness it
400	 *   caused (e.g. ketoacidosis) is still a problem.
401	 */
402	export interface ProblemRow {
403	  /** The condition as the source words it, e.g. "Chronic kidney disease stage 3a". */
404	  condition: string;
405	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot, as the source gives it (latest). Omit if the source gives none. */
406	  icd10cm?: string;
407	  /** SNOMED CT concept id, if the source gives one. */
408	  snomed?: string;
409	  /**
410	   * - 'active': the patient has it.
411	   * - 'resolved': the patient had it and the source says it is resolved or historical.
412	   */
413	  status: 'active' | 'resolved';
414	  /** When the condition began, at the precision the source knows. Omit if the source does not say. */
415	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
416	  /**
417	   * For chronic kidney disease only: the KDIGO GFR category the source most recently recorded for this
418	   * patient ('G3a' for "stage 3a", "N18.31" or a G3a category field). As recorded by a clinician; never
419	   * computed from lab values.
420	   */
421	  ckd_stage?: 'G1' | 'G2' | 'G3a' | 'G3b' | 'G4' | 'G5';
422	  /** For chronic kidney disease only: KDIGO albuminuria category as recorded ('A1', 'A2', 'A3'), if the source records one. */
423	  albuminuria?: 'A1' | 'A2' | 'A3';
424	  evidence: Evidence;
425	}

427	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
428	// Allergies, intolerances, adverse reactions
429	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
430	
431	/**
432	 * One substance the patient should avoid or be careful with, as of `asOf`. Only current entries: an
433	 * entry the source marks inactive or invalid is not reported. "No known drug allergies" is not a row.
434	 */
435	export interface AllergyIntoleranceRow {
436	  /** Substance: generic ingredient name, lower case, for drugs ("lisinopril"); as written otherwise. */
437	  substance: string;
438	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, if the source gives one. */
439	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
440	  /**
441	   * What kind of reaction, by its nature (not by which list the source keeps it on):
442	   * - 'allergy': immune-mediated (hives, rash, angioedema, anaphylaxis, bronchospasm).
443	   * - 'intolerance': a non-immune, predictable side effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g.
444	   *   ACE-inhibitor cough, GI upset).
445	   * - 'adverse_reaction': a serious harmful event attributed to the drug that is not an allergy (e.g.
446	   *   drug-associated ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis).
447	   * If the source keeps all three on one undifferentiated list, decide from the recorded reaction.
448	   */
449	  type: 'allergy' | 'intolerance' | 'adverse_reaction';
450	  /** Reaction(s) as the source words them, joined with "; ". Omit if not recorded. */
451	  reaction?: string;
452	  /**
453	   * Criticality: how dangerous re-exposure is judged to be.
454	   * - 'high': re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening.
455	   * - 'low': re-exposure unlikely to cause serious harm.
456	   * - 'unknown': not assessed or not derivable.
457	   * A source's "severity" scale is mapped by meaning: mild -> 'low'; severe or life-threatening -> 'high'.
458	   */
459	  criticality: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
460	  /** When the reaction began, at the precision the source knows. */
461	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
462	  evidence: Evidence;
463	}
464	
465	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
466	// Lab results
467	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
468	
469	/**
470	 * Analytes this consumer tracks, with the unit `LabResultRow.value` must be in. Results for other
471	 * tests are not reported.
472	 *
473	 * | analyte         | unit            | notes |
474	 * |-----------------|-----------------|-------|
475	 * | creatinine      | mg/dL           | serum |
476	 * | egfr            | mL/min/1.73m2   | see `egfr_equation` and the eGFR rule below |
477	 * | potassium       | mmol/L          | |
478	 * | sodium          | mmol/L          | |
479	 * | chloride        | mmol/L          | |
480	 * | bicarbonate     | mmol/L          | total CO2 |
481	 * | anion_gap       | mmol/L          | |
482	 * | bun             | mg/dL           | urea nitrogen |
483	 * | glucose         | mg/dL           | laboratory glucose (serum/plasma); home meter readings are vitals |
484	 * | a1c             | %               | NGSP |
485	 * | uacr            | mg/g            | urine albumin/creatinine ratio |
486	 * | platelets       | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre: 212 000 cells/uL is 212 |
487	 * | wbc             | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre |
488	 * | hemoglobin      | g/dL            | |
489	 * | bhb             | mmol/L          | beta-hydroxybutyrate |
490	 * | ph              | [pH]            | blood gas pH |
491	 * | pco2            | mmHg            | |
492	 * | lipase          | U/L             | |
493	 * | troponin        | ng/mL           | troponin I |
494	 * | cholesterol     | mg/dL           | total |
495	 * | triglycerides   | mg/dL           | |
496	 * | hdl             | mg/dL           | |
497	 * | ldl             | mg/dL           | measured or calculated |
498	 */
499	export type Analyte =
500	  | 'creatinine' | 'egfr' | 'potassium' | 'sodium' | 'chloride' | 'bicarbonate' | 'anion_gap' | 'bun'
501	  | 'glucose' | 'a1c' | 'uacr' | 'platelets' | 'wbc' | 'hemoglobin' | 'bhb' | 'ph' | 'pco2' | 'lipase'
502	  | 'troponin' | 'cholesterol' | 'triglycerides' | 'hdl' | 'ldl';
503	
504	/**
505	 * One valid laboratory result.
506	 *
507	 * - One row per result. A result the source shows several times (copies in several documents, a
508	 *   preliminary and a final copy) is one row, taken from the copy with the most advanced status.
509	 * - Report only values that stand: leave out results that were withdrawn, invalidated or "corrected
510	 *   away" by the lab, results of orders voided or entered in error, results not performed, and
511	 *   superseded copies. A confirmation repeat is a second valid result; keep both.
512	 * - **eGFR rule.** One eGFR row per eGFR calculation the source reports for a specimen. When the source
513	 *   reports race-specific variants of one calculation (a value with and one without a race
514	 *   coefficient), report only the variant without the race coefficient. Report the value as printed
515	 *   (do not recompute).
516	 */
517	export interface LabResultRow {
518	  analyte: Analyte;
519	  /** Numeric value in the analyte's unit (see `Analyte`). For a result printed with a comparator (">60", "<0.01"), the number part. */
520	  value: number;
521	  /** Set when the printed result has a comparator: ">60" -> value 60, comparator '>'. */
522	  comparator?: '<' | '>' | '<=' | '>=';
523	  /** The analyte's unit from the table in `Analyte`, exactly as written there. */
524	  unit: string;
525	  /** Specimen collection time, RFC 3339 with offset (any offset; it denotes an instant). */
526	  collected: string;
527	  /** 'final' (also for amended or corrected values that stand) or 'preliminary'. */
528	  status: 'final' | 'preliminary';
529	  /**
530	   * For analyte 'egfr' only: the equation the source says it used.
531	   * - 'ckd-epi-2021': CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free).
532	   * - 'ckd-epi-2009': CKD-EPI 2009.
533	   * - 'mdrd': MDRD.
534	   * - 'unknown': not stated.
535	   * When a code and a method note disagree, believe the method note.
536	   */
537	  egfr_equation?: 'ckd-epi-2021' | 'ckd-epi-2009' | 'mdrd' | 'unknown';
538	  /** LOINC code if the source gives one for this result. */
539	  loinc?: string;
540	  evidence: Evidence;
541	}
542	
543	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
544	// Vital signs and home readings
545	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
546	
547	/**
548	 * One set of vital signs taken together, or one home reading.
549	 *
550	 * - A clinic or hospital vital-sign set (BP, pulse, weight taken within a few minutes at one visit) is
551	 *   one row; `local_time` is the time of its first blood pressure (or of its first measurement if no
552	 *   BP). A repeat blood pressure taken later in the same visit goes in `repeat_*` on the same row.
553	 * - Each home BP reading and each home glucose reading is its own row.
554	 * - Each measurement is reported once: if a source shows the same measurement twice (a reading typed
555	 *   in by hand that duplicates one synced from the device a minute or two earlier with the same
556	 *   values), report it once, preferring the device copy.
557	 */
558	export interface VitalRow {
559	  /** 'clinic' (outpatient office), 'hospital' (ED or inpatient), or 'home' (patient's own devices). */
560	  setting: 'clinic' | 'hospital' | 'home';
561	  /** Local wall-clock time in America/Chicago, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. */
562	  local_time: string;
563	  systolic_mmhg?: number;
564	  diastolic_mmhg?: number;
565	  /** Repeat blood pressure at the same visit, if one was taken. */
566	  repeat_systolic_mmhg?: number;
567	  repeat_diastolic_mmhg?: number;
568	  pulse_bpm?: number;
569	  /** Body weight in kilograms (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg), one decimal place. */
570	  weight_kg?: number;
571	  /** Home glucose meter reading in mg/dL (1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL), rounded to a whole number. */
572	  glucose_mg_dl?: number;
573	  /** Set when the meter showed HI or LO instead of a number; `glucose_mg_dl` is then the meter's limit in mg/dL. */
574	  glucose_out_of_range?: 'HI' | 'LO';
575	  evidence: Evidence;
576	}

I wrote `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks and runs on the sample patients. It returns only medications and home vitals. The other views are empty because the source has no problems, allergies or labs. I only read the sample output for the first patient and part of the second, so the third patient's rows haven't been checked.

**Judgment calls**
- **Scope and corrections:** I treat an item as in scope if its `recorded` time falls on or before `asOf` in America/Chicago. Anything named in an in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` is dropped, which also covers chains of supersession.
- **Time zone:** HomeLog stores phone wall-clock time with no zone. The consumer displays Chicago time and the source gives nothing else, so I pass `measured_at` through as Chicago local time.
- **Medications:** I use only the latest in-scope My Medicines list, and a drug missing from it is not reported.
- **Ingredient names:**
  - If the patient picked the drug from search, I take the ingredient from the display text and strip salts like "potassium".
  - Otherwise I use a built-in brand/generic table.
  - If a name isn't in the table (for example "water pill"), I leave the ingredient out.
  - I only set the RxNorm code when the picked item is ingredient-level (no strength in the display text).
- **Duplicate ingredients:** I keep one row per ingredient, choosing the entry with the latest stop date, or start date if it has none.
- **Status:** "taking" becomes active and "stopped" becomes stopped. A stopped drug whose note reads like a pause ("on hold", "until", "temporarily") becomes held, because the schema says patients record pauses as stopped. A stop reason is set only when the note matches obvious keywords.
- **Dose and frequency:**
  - Dose is read from `how_i_take_it` when it states an amount, such as "10 units at bedtime".
  - A bare leading count is multiplied by the tablet strength, so "2 … 200 mg" becomes 400 mg.
  - Otherwise dose is the mg/mcg strength.
  - A "units/mL" strength is not a dose.
  - Frequency comes from keywords in the patient's text. "When my back hurts" is PRN, even though the same text says "a few times a week".
  - Doses are as the patient wrote them. For example, "Synthroid 75 mg" stays 75 mg and is not corrected to mcg.
- **Vitals:**
  - Each BP and each glucose reading is its own home row.
  - mmol/L is converted at 18.016 and rounded.
  - HI/LO is passed through.
  - A typed reading within 3 minutes of a device reading with the same values is dropped in favour of the device copy.
- **Not mapped:** Dose-log entries and diary notes produce no rows, because no view takes them.
